propertiesNote: 3-row aggregation by Australian growing region. Total 22,403 planted acres across Sunraysia/Vic, SA Riverland, and NSW Riverina.

properties.name: Sunraysia / Robinvale region (Victoria)
properties.fmvRationale: Sunraysia / Robinvale is Australia's primary almond growing region; mature orchards 2024-25 trade at $25-32K AUD/acre. SHV's Carina West processing hub anchors this cluster

properties.name: Riverland / Loxton / Paringa region (South Australia)
properties.fmvRationale: SA Riverland almond orchards; slightly below Sunraysia per-acre due to water-cost differential (SA water rights more expensive)

properties.name: Riverina region (NSW)

comparables.source: Colliers Rural + LAWD H1 2025 ag-real-estate report

comparables.description: Select Harvests Piangil acquisition (Sunraysia almond orchards) at $129M; per-acre derived from acquired hectares

methodology:
Select Harvests is Australia's largest pure-play almond grower. The 22,403-acre planted portfolio spans three growing regions: Sunraysia/Victoria (Robinvale, Piangil) — the largest cluster and home to the Carina West processing facility; SA Riverland (Loxton, Paringa); and NSW Riverina.

FY25 (year ended Sep 30, 2025) was a strong year — revenue jumped 35% to A$398M and EBITDA jumped 81% to A$82M as almond prices rose ($10.18/kg vs $7.69 prior year). The land FMV reflects current Australian almond orchard transaction prices (2024-25 Colliers Rural / LAWD reports show $30-35K AUD/acre for mature Sunraysia ground).

Net debt of A$168M (1H FY25) is higher leverage than peer farmland operators, reflecting Select Harvests' use of debt to fund the Piangil acquisition. Live-price-vs-FMV-NAV will reflect the leverage drag.

Per-region splits use rough estimates of SHV's geographic mix. The company doesn't publicly disclose orchard acres by region — refining against their FY25 annual report (released November 2025) would tighten the per-region numbers.

The $28K/acre Sunraysia anchor matches the implied price of SHV's own 2024 Piangil acquisition (A$129M). SA Riverland is marked slightly lower at $25K/acre to reflect higher water entitlement costs in SA vs. Vic.
